headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared filesystem plus broad egress; no direct evidence of stronger pairwise hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, while Plane handles uploaded files and notes. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Plane content is copied into Mentat’s workspace. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles and kept at medium.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied into a Mentat-managed file or diff input, Mentat may parse attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF the two agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, file content can bridge them without provenance checks.
mitigations: Keep Plane exports and Mentat workspaces in separate directories.
Review any Plane-derived text before placing it into Mentat inputs.
Use read-only copies for cross-agent handoff files.
Add a manual provenance note to shared files.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and sends content to a configured model provider, while Plane accepts file uploads and stores issues, tasks, notes, and files. If sensitive Plane data is fed into Mentat, it can leave the local environment through the model backend. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive Plane files or notes are passed into Mentat, they may be transmitted to the configured model provider.
IF both agents are used on the same project data, Plane artifacts can be exposed through Mentat prompts or diffs.
mitigations: Do not paste sensitive Plane content into Mentat prompts.
Use redacted copies of Plane exports for coding tasks.
Restrict Mentat to non-sensitive repositories.
Verify model-provider retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on cross-agent file handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state; Plane is not writable locally but can ingest files and operate on shared project artifacts. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources such as the same repo or workspace, where Mentat’s edits can race with Plane-managed files or exports. No locking is documented, so the overlap is material.
conditions: IF Plane and Mentat target the same repository or workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Plane-generated files are edited by Mentat without locking, stale writes can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
Use git branches for Mentat changes.
Manually reconcile diffs before syncing to Plane.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Plane can store tasks, notes, and issue content that may be treated as authoritative project input. If Plane output is fed into Mentat or Mentat edits are copied back into Plane without review, errors can cascade across work products. The profiles do not show automatic verification, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Plane task text is used as authoritative input to Mentat, incorrect requirements can propagate into code edits.
IF Mentat diffs are copied into Plane without human review, downstream task records can become stale or wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before copying outputs between agents.
Cross-check Mentat diffs against Plane source tasks.
Mark Plane items as draft until verified.
Keep a changelog of handoffs between agents.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between task text and code diffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention constraints. Plane exposes support channels and file uploads, while Mentat uses a model provider API key, but no specific compliance mismatch is documented. Because the relevant policies are absent rather than aligned, the risk stays low and only one-agent citations are needed.
conditions: IF sensitive data is routed through Plane support channels or Mentat model-provider calls, local policy may need review.
IF an operator requires a specific residency or retention guarantee, the profiles do not document it.
mitigations: Confirm internal data-handling policy before use.
Avoid sending regulated data through support channels.
Review model-provider retention settings.
Document the approved data classes for each agent.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations from vendors.
